Dear Sir/Madam, Sub: Intimation regarding 34th Annual General Meeting (“AGM”) of Coforge Limited, e-voting, Notice of AGM This is in continuation to letter dated July 29, 2026, wherein the Company intimated about the ensuing 34th Annual General Meeting (AGM) of the Members of the Company scheduled to be held on Monday, August 24, 2026 at 05:00 P.M. (IST) through Video Conferencing /Other Audio Visual Means (VC/OAVM), without the physical presence of members at a common venue, in compliance with MCA & SEBI Circulars. Pursuant to provisions of Section 108 of the Companies Act, 2013 and Rule 20 of the Companies (Management and Administration) Rules, 2014, as amended and Regulation 44 of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements), Regulations, 2015 (“SEBI Listing Regulations”), the Company is pleased to provide members the facility to exercise their right to vote at the ensuing AGM by electronic means and the business may be transacted through e- Voting Services. The facility of casting the votes by the members using an electronic voting system from a place other than venue of the AGM (“remote e-voting”) will be provided by National Securities Depository Limited (NSDL). The facility for voting through remote e-voting shall also be made available at the AGM. The Notice is also available on the website of the Company (www.coforge.com) and National Securities Depository Limited (NSDL), www.evoting.nsdl.com inter alia indicating the process and manner of e-voting process. The e-voting period begins on Friday, August 21, 2026, at 09:00 A.M. (IST) and ends on Sunday, August 23, 2026, at 05:00 P.M. (IST). During this period shareholders of the Company may cast their vote electronically. The e-voting module shall also be disabled for voting thereafter.

Once the vote on a resolution is cast by the shareholder, the shareholder shall not be allowed to change it subsequently. The voting rights of members shall be in proportion to their shares of the paid-up equity share capital of the Company as on the cut-off date of Monday, August 17, 2026. Any person, who acquires shares of the Company and become member of the Company after dispatch of the notice and holding shares as on the cut-off date may obtain the login ID and password by sending a request at evoting@nsdl.com or investor.helpdesk@in.mpms.mufg.com or investors@Coforge.com Further, in compliance with Regulation 34 of the SEBI Listing Regulations, please find attached the copy of Notice of AGM for your information and records. In terms of MCA Circulars, the Company has made arrangements with its Registrar & Share Transfer Agent for registration of email addresses of those shareholders who have not yet registered their email address. Those shareholders are requested to get their email addresses registered by following the procedure given in notes to the Notice of AGM. This is for your information and records. Thanking you, Yours truly, For Coforge Limited Barkha Sharma Company Secretary & Compliance Officer Encl.: As above

Corporate Profile
WHO WE ARE
We pride ourselves on strong employee engagement, resulting in a 10.8% attrition rate: one of the lowest levels and a testament to our company culture.
We have a robust set of AI assets and industry-domain focused AI solutions. Our AI specialists work with large enterprises to design and deliver enterprise-grade agentic AI solutions.
We lead with capabilities in AI-led engineering, cloud, and data technologies to help clients evolve into intelligent, high-growth enterprises.

We lead with capabilities in AI-led engineering, cloud, and data technologies to help clients evolve into intelligent, high-growth enterprises.
We are a global AI-native engineering services leader, where AI is the very foundation of how we design, build, and deliver intelligent solutions for our clients. We use AI and hyperspecialized industry expertise to engineer autonomous enterprises.
This employee centricity was demonstrated again in 2026, when Coforge was recognized as a “Great Place to Work” for the sixth consecutive year. We were also among the ET Edge Best Organisations for Women in 2026.
Coforge Nuuron, our AI operationalization platform, transforms enterprise knowledge, business context, and decision logic into an operational intelligence layer, helping enterprises deploy agentic AI solutions at scale with the necessary guardrails for compliance and risk management.
Our mission is to “Transform at the Intersect,” helping our customers achieve their business objectives by combining our deep expertise in both technology and domain. We have applied this approach to provide business solutions within our chosen industry verticals: Banking and Financial Services, Insurance, Travel, Public Sector (outside India), Hi-Tech, and Healthcare.

At Coforge, we believe that the leaders of tomorrow will have their business capabilities defined and executed by a combination of humans and agents, underpinned by an enterprise data core and a cloud foundation purpose-built for AI.
LOOKING FORWARD
• Our CodeInsightAI platform is a proven legacy modernization tool.
As the shift to agentic AI continues, the most successful enterprises will harness intelligent systems to drive autonomous decisions. This means that AI platforms will be measured by how much they can be trusted, and value will be measured by the outcomes they deliver.
COFORGE TODAY
We combine AI agents with our AI-enabled workforce, including specialized FDEs in hybrid, pod-based delivery units. With a deep focus on trusted AI, our solutions are secure, governed, and enterprise-grade.
• Our BlueSwan® platform is an end-to-end AI-driven quality engineering platform.
We have a global presence across North America, South America, Europe, the Middle East, India, Asia-Pacific, and Australia. We drive operations from 54 global delivery centers across 32 countries. As of June 30th, 2026, we had over 40,000 AI engineers, technology and process experts who design, engineer, modernize, and operate client systems across the world.

• Our EvolveOps.AI offering is an autonomous cloud infrastructure management platform that 37 of our clients are currently using to deploy AI agents for automated cloud operations.
We are outcome-led by design. Moving beyond AI experimentation, we deliver measurable business outcomes: lower operating costs, faster cycle times, higher conversion rates, and sustained margin growth.
We are already building our business for that future.
Coforge will continue our evolution to an AI-first, engineering-led enterprise, expanding our investments in next-generation delivery platforms, foundational agents, and hyper-specialized solutions built for the industries we serve. We will deepen our ecosystem partnerships to co-create high-impact solutions with the best in the industry, while cultivating an adaptable, agile, and AI-ready talent pool to face tomorrow’s challenges.
We are focused and committed to our clients’ success, as reflected in our repeat business rate of 95% in FY26. We have an exceptional track record of execution, which has been a key enabler of robust and consistent revenue growth over the last nine years from INR 27,558Mn in FY17 to INR 1,64,027Mn in FY26, with a 20.3% CAGR over this period.
• Our agentic AI data assets enable data modernization, cloud migration and data ops.

People and Culture

• By turning intelligence into action, Coforge Nuuron enables a new model of enterprise operations - adaptive, autonomous, and outcome-driven.
2. An AI-native talent and delivery model. In FY26, we trained more than 30,000 engineers on AI technologies and delivery practices, creating one of the industry’s largest pools of AI-enabled engineering talent. At its leading edge is our specialized team of Forward Deployed Engineers who work alongside clients to rapidly identify opportunities, build solutions, and accelerate value realization. Complementing this is Mod Squads, our subscription-based delivery model that combines specialist engineering talent, pre-built AI agents, and reusable IP into dedicated outcome-focused teams. Together, these capabilities enable clients to move from idea to production faster, while maintaining a relentless focus on business outcomes rather than effort-based delivery.
Outlook
Another Exceptional Year of Industry-Leading Growth

Another Exceptional Year of Industry-Leading Growth
Looking ahead, we remain laser-focused on extending our growth leadership into FY27 and beyond, anchored in our differentiated capabilities and execution intensity. The technology services industry is at an inflection point, where the capabilities that define a leader are being rewritten in real time, and we intend to be one of the organizations doing the rewriting. Our Forward Deployed Engineer model, our Coforge Nuuron platform, and our conviction that clients will increasingly buy outcomes rather than capacity are not side bets; they are the operating logic of Coforge going forward.
Dear Shareholders,

Dear Shareholders,
FY26 was a defining year for Coforge, not only because of the growth and profitability we delivered, but because of how we delivered it. The technology services industry is going through a genuine shift in its business model: from a scale-of-people business to a scale-of- intelligence one, where how many people you can deploy matters less than the intelligence and judgment you bring to a client’s problem. Clients are moving away from paying for effort and toward paying for outcomes, risk reduced, revenue unlocked, value delivered on their terms. Our Forward Deployed Engineers (FDE) program is where this shows up most clearly: we embed elite, AI- fluent engineers directly inside client environments, compressing the distance between problem and solution from months to weeks. This is the front line of our AI strategy, and it is changing how Coforge competes.

Our FY26 EBIT margin was 14.4%, up 370 basis points, driven in large part by the programmatic use of AI to lift the efficiency of our own internal operations. We do not just sell AI transformation. We run on it ourselves.

We remain confident of robust, sustainable growth in the years ahead, and determined to emerge from this AI era even stronger, as one of the planet’s most trusted innovation and transformation partners for enterprises. The conversation around AI is often centered on models, platforms and tools; at Coforge, we see it in a broader sense, as a force multiplier for human potential, enabling our people to work smarter, deliver faster and create more meaningful impact for our clients. That is the Coforge we are building, and I have never been more confident in our ability to get there.
3. Speed of value realization. Our Outcome Acceleration Framework is designed to shorten the path from AI deployment to measurable business impact. The biggest challenge is rarely the technology itself but embedding it into the way people work. An underwriting agent delivers little value if underwriters do not use it. A customer service copilot has limited impact if agents are not enabled and measured to adopt it. That is why we integrate workflow redesign, adoption, governance, and value measurement alongside the technology from day one. By treating these as a single workstream aligned to business outcomes, we help clients move beyond pilots faster and realize value with greater speed, predictability, and scale.

We also took a significant step toward our AI ambition this year with the acquisition of Encora, an AI-native engineering firm born in Silicon Valley. Together, Coforge and Encora will form a combined entity which will derive more than USD 2 billion in revenue from AI- led engineering, Data and Cloud services alone. That differentiated core sets the foundation that will help us realize the potential of AI for enterprise clients across the world.
Against this backdrop, FY26 was another exceptional year for Coforge, marked by industry-leading growth, sharply improved profitability, and continued progress on our long-term priorities. We delivered revenue growth of 29.2% over FY25 in USD terms, our second consecutive year of industry-leading growth, and our ninth consecutive year of robust, profitable growth overall. Over FY17 to FY26, revenue has grown at a CAGR of 20.3% and EBIT at a CAGR of 24.6% in INR terms, a class-leading performance that has continued to accelerate even as our base has scaled.

Business Overview
FY26 represents a year of strong execution and increasing strategic momentum for Coforge, as the Company continues to scale its presence in large, transformation-led engagements across key markets. Growth during the year was driven by consistent deal wins, expansion within existing accounts, and participation in complex, multi-year programs aligned with enterprise modernization priorities. The Company maintained its growth trajectory on the back of a robust order pipeline and a high-quality executable order book of USD 1.75 billion for the next twelve months as of Q4 FY26, reflecting a 16.4% year-over-year (YOY) increase.

Coforge operates as a focused, AI-native engineering services leader, differentiated by its deep domain specialization, its engineering-led delivery model, and consistent execution in complex, large-scale transformation programs. The Company’s positioning is anchored in its ability to combine industry context with engineering depth, enabling it to deliver measurable business outcomes rather than effort-led services. Coforge continues to build on a strong foundation of sustained, high-quality growth, reinforcing its position as one of the fastest-growing digital engineering firms in the industry. The Company’s performance is underpinned by a focused strategy, consistent execution, and an increasing ability to participate in large, transformation-led engagements across key markets. Over the years, the Company has evolved from a traditional technology services provider into a strategic transformation partner, helping clients solve complex, domain-specific challenges by integrating advanced technologies with deep industry expertise.

The acquisition of Encora further strengthens Coforge’s digital engineering capabilities and expands its global delivery footprint, particularly in near-shore markets. Encora enhances access to specialized engineering talent and new client segments, while enabling deeper participation across the engineering lifecycle from advisory and design to build and run. Its strong focus on digital product engineering and AI-led development capabilities complements Coforge’s AI-first strategy, accelerating the Company’s ability to deliver next-generation, AI-powered engineering solutions at scale. Together, these acquisitions position Coforge to deliver end-to-end transformation programs with greater agility, depth, and sustained value creation.

As enterprise adoption of AI moves from experimentation to production, clients are prioritizing partners who can take end- to-end ownership of systems, including their ongoing operation, governance, and optimization. This is expanding the scope of engagements toward long-duration, managed services-led programs with higher value realization over time. Coforge’s AI- led engineering approach, supported by a growing portfolio of proprietary platforms, accelerators, and domain-centric IP, has been a key enabler of this shift. These capabilities are being embedded across the lifecycle of engagements to accelerate modernization, improve delivery productivity, and enhance outcome predictability. Rather than being positioned as standalone solutions, these assets are increasingly driving differentiation in large deal pursuits, enabling faster time-to-value and supporting Coforge’s ability to execute complex, transformation-led programs at scale.

Coforge’s growth is anchored in three structural strengths. First, a deeply embedded execution discipline that drives consistency, predictability, and delivery excellence across engagements. Second, a strong large-deal engine focused on solution-led, multi- year managed services programs, enabling the Company to expand wallet share and participate in strategic client initiatives. Third, a differentiated domain-led engineering approach, built on deep industry specialization, which allows Coforge to address complex, context-specific business challenges with precision.
Coforge enters FY27 with enhanced visibility and confidence in its growth trajectory, supported by a USD 1.75 billion executable order book, a healthy large-deal pipeline, and increased participation in strategic transformation programs. A focused emphasis on high-quality engagements, outcome-driven delivery, and long-term client partnerships has resulted in improved revenue predictability, stronger client stickiness, and a more resilient growth profile.

As enterprise adoption evolves from early generative AI use cases to more advanced, agentic, and autonomous systems, Coforge is positioned to capture this opportunity by embedding AI across the full lifecycle of client engagements. The Company’s platforms, including Data Cosmos, CodeInsightAI, Coforge QuasarTM, AI Studio, Coforge AgentSphereTM, GenAI Central, and Trust AI, are enabling scalable and responsible AI adoption, driving productivity gains and faster time-to-value while ensuring governance, security, and enterprise-grade reliability.

The executable order book stood at USD 1.75 billion over the next twelve months as of Q4 FY26, reflecting a 16.4% YoY increase and providing strong visibility into near-term growth.

As the Company moves into FY27, it does so from a position of strength. The strategic focus remains on scaling AI-powered solutions, expanding client wallet share, and delivering margin- accretive growth through disciplined execution. With a strong executable order book, a resilient and diversified client base, and a differentiated portfolio aligned to the evolving technology landscape, Coforge is well-positioned to sustain its growth momentum. FY26, in this context, represents a significant milestone that strengthens the foundation for the Company’s next phase of growth and its continued journey toward building intelligent, high-growth enterprises for its clients while creating long-term stakeholder value.
Client engagement remains a core strength. Coforge serves a diversified base of 260 clients, including 61 Forbes Global 1000 organizations, and continues to generate a high repeat business rate of 95.5%. Coforge’s long-standing relationships are evidenced by an average tenure of more than 10 years with its top 10 clients, reflecting deep integration into client operations and sustained trust.

The integration of Cigniti Technologies represents a meaningful acceleration in Coforge’s growth and operating model, strengthening both capability depth and deal participation across large, enterprise-scale programs. More importantly, the integration is beginning to unlock strategic cross-sell opportunities across Coforge’s client base. While the initial performance has been driven largely by standalone momentum, the cross-leverage between Coforge’s engineering-led capabilities and Cigniti’s leadership in quality engineering is expanding deal sizes and increasing participation in multi-tower transformation programs. This combination enables Coforge to offer a more integrated value proposition across engineering, modernization, and AI- led assurance, which is increasingly critical for enterprise-scale transformation. AI and Engineering as a Core Strategy

AI and Engineering as a Core Strategy
The technology services industry is undergoing a structural realignment, as enterprise demand shifts from effort-based delivery toward engineering-led, AI-enabled value creation. This shift is redefining the basis of competitiveness, from scaling capacity to scaling outcomes, with an increasing emphasis on the ability to design, modernize, operate complex systems with precision, control, and continuity. As AI becomes integral to the technology stack, the primary driver of value is moving from development to lifecycle ownership, where governance, orchestration, and continuous optimization determine long-term impact.
A key differentiator in this strategy is the integration of platforms with deep domain specialization. Coforge’s focus on select industries ensures that its AI and engineering capabilities are applied within real-world business contexts, regulatory environments, and operational workflows. This allows the Company to move beyond pilot-led AI adoption to production-scale, outcome-driven deployments across core enterprise systems.

A defining element of Coforge’s alliance strategy is its early and deliberate alignment with the multi-model AI ecosystem. As enterprises increasingly adopt a portfolio approach to AI spanning multiple large language model (LLM) providers, Coforge enables seamless orchestration across models through Coforge Quasar™ platform, which acts as a control plane for multi-LLM integration, governance, and cost optimization. This approach ensures that clients retain flexibility, avoid vendor lock-in, and optimize AI adoption strategies based on workload-specific requirements.

The Company is also evolving its commercial model to reflect this shift. As AI changes the economics of delivery, the person-hour is becoming a less relevant unit of value creation. Coforge’s platform- led and AI-augmented delivery constructs enable more modular, subscription-based, and outcome-linked models, improving alignment with client value while enhancing non-linearity in its own delivery engine. Constructs such as AI-powered Mod Squads further support this transition by combining domain-aligned engineering expertise with pre-built AI agents to deliver faster, more predictable outcomes. Importantly, Coforge’s model is designed to capture value across the full lifecycle of AI systems. As enterprises deploy agentic architectures at scale, the complexity of managing models, orchestrating agents, ensuring governance, and continuously optimizing systems creates a structurally expanding managed services opportunity. Coforge is positioned to own this layer through its platforms and engineering capabilities, extending its role from implementation to long-term lifecycle partner.

The second pillar is platformization and IP-led differentiation, where Coforge continues to industrialize its delivery through reusable assets, accelerators, and domain-specific AI solutions. With more than 50 AI accelerators, 300+ enterprise AI deployments, and a robust portfolio spanning CodeInsightAI, BlueSwan®, and EvolveOps.AI, Coforge is embedding intelligence across the entire lifecycle from design to run. This platform-led approach not only compresses time-to-market but also ensures consistency, scalability, and predictable value realization across engagements.
In this environment, the distinction between linear delivery models and engineering-led execution is becoming increasingly pronounced. Enterprises are prioritizing partners that can move beyond program execution to assume accountability for system outcomes across build, run, and evolution. Coforge operates within this paradigm, with a delivery model architected to integrate AI into the core of engineering, enabling consistent execution at scale across complex, domain-intensive environments.

Beyond hyperscalers, Coforge has built a layered ecosystem of enterprise platform partnerships that embed AI directly into business workflows. Strategic collaborations with Salesforce, ServiceNow, Appian, Snowflake, Databricks, and integration platforms such as Workato and SnapLogic enable Coforge to deliver end-to-end, AI-infused transformation across customer experience, operations, data, and enterprise systems. These partnerships are increasingly structured around joint solutioning and co-developed accelerators, enabling Coforge to integrate domain-specific intelligence directly into enterprise platforms.
A third critical pillar is deep domain specialization combined with large deal focus, enabling Coforge to operate as a transformation partner rather than a transactional vendor. The Company’s industry-aligned model across banking and financial services, insurance, travel, healthcare & life sciences, hi-tech, and public sector enables it to co-create solutions that are deeply embedded in client workflows. This has translated into strong large-deal momentum, with consistent multi-million-dollar deal closures across geographies and a growing base of long-tenured, high-value client relationships that drive repeat business and wallet share expansion.

AI is now a foundational layer across the engineering lifecycle, enabling a transition from manual, artifact-driven processes to platform-enabled, agent-assisted execution. AI is embedded into modernization, development, quality engineering, and operations, driving a structural redesign of how enterprise systems are engineered and managed. The resulting model delivers not only improvements in productivity and cycle time, but also greater reliability, traceability, and operational control, which are critical to scaling AI in production environments.
Coforge’s partnership model is further strengthened by its focus on co-innovation and IP-led collaboration. The Company actively works with hyperscalers and platform partners to build joint accelerators, industry-specific agentic solutions, and reusable AI frameworks, significantly reducing deployment timelines while enhancing solution differentiation. This includes co-innovation initiatives such as the GenAI Center of Excellence (CoE) with ServiceNow, combining Coforge QuasarTM with Now Assist to accelerate enterprise AI adoption. This approach transforms partnerships from enablement channels into multipliers of innovation velocity and deal origination.

This strategy is underpinned by Coforge’s consistent emphasis on execution intensity and hyper-specialization. The Company’s ability to combine domain expertise with disciplined execution has been a key driver of its growth, and this continues to define how AI and engineering capabilities are operationalized across engagements.
At the center of this model is a platform-led execution architecture, where Coforge’s proprietary platforms and accelerators are deeply integrated into delivery. The Company’s One AI platform stack, including Coforge Quasar™, Coforge Forge-X™, CodeInsightAI, BlueSwan®, AIVA, Coforge Data Cosmos™, and EvolveOps.AI, acts as a unified engineering and AI fabric that enables industrialized transformation across the enterprise. This stack aligns with the Company’s broader AI value proposition across AI for Business and AI for Delivery, enabling enterprise-wide adoption while accelerating transformation delivery at scale.

The fourth pillar centers on scalable AI infrastructure and ecosystem-led growth, where Coforge is making deliberate investments in owned compute, multi-model architectures, and hyperscaler partnerships. By combining sovereign AI infrastructure, open-source models, and frontier LLM ecosystems, Coforge ensures cost optimization, model flexibility, and enterprise-grade governance. This multi-layered AI stack enables Coforge to deploy AI at scale while avoiding vendor lock-in, thereby strengthening its positioning as a long-term transformation partner in enterprise AI adoption.
Overall, Coforge is building a scaled AI-led engineering enterprise, where proprietary platforms, domain depth, execution rigor, and an AI-enabled workforce come together to deliver measurable business outcomes. This positions the Company strongly in a market that is increasingly rewarding firms capable of translating AI into real, production-grade impact.

The acquisition of Encora represents a strategic acceleration of this ecosystem-driven approach. Encora brings deep hyperscaler relationships, AI-native engineering capabilities, and the AIVA composable agentic AI platform architecture, enhancing Coforge’s ability to deliver large-scale, AI-led transformation programs across geographies. The combined entity strengthens Coforge’s positioning as a scaled AI-led engineering firm with a robust ecosystem backbone spanning hyperscalers, data platforms, and AI frameworks.

A designated green area in Sector 108, Noida, had become a garbage dumping site. In August 2023, Coforge stepped in as a sponsor and cleared 22 truckloads of waste. Nearly 500 Coforge employees then planted 10,000 trees, transforming the area into a biodiversity park and a carbon-absorbing ecosystem. On 12 March 2026, Coforge volunteers from the Greater Noida campus returned to the site to plant 1,000 additional saplings. The site was further enhanced with a water body to support birds, insects, and small animals, along with two insect hotels designed to aid insect survival. Information flow to the Board
The Board receives information on an ongoing basis for review, input, and approval. It considers the Company’s annual strategic and operating plans, while quarterly and annual financial statements are reviewed first by the Audit Committee and then placed before the Board for approval. Matters such as business performance, appointment of Directors and Key Managerial Personnel, corporate actions, audit reviews, investor grievances, acquisitions, significant management decisions, material developments, risk management initiatives, legal matters, and statutory compliance are placed before the relevant Committees and, where required, submitted to the Board with their recommendations. Documents containing Unpublished Price Sensitive Information may, where necessary, be circulated to Board and Committee members at shorter notice in accordance with the Board’s general consent. As Directors are located across geographies, the Company provides video conferencing and other audio-visual facilities to support effective remote participation and decision-making. After each Board meeting, the Company tracks, reviews, and reports management action taken on decisions of the Board and its Committees.

Cash flow hedging reserve
The Company uses hedging instruments as part of its management of foreign currency risk associated with its highly probable forecasted transactions, i.e., revenue, as described within Note 27. The Company’s exposure to the risk of changes in foreign exchange rates relates primarily to the Company’s operating activities (when revenue or expense is denominated in a foreign currency) and the Company’s net investments in foreign subsidiaries.
The Company manages its foreign currency risk by hedging transactions that are expected to occur within a maximum 12-month period for hedges of forecasted sales.

During previous year, a complaint has been filed against Coforge Inc. (Group Company) and Coforge Limited (the Company) by named plaintiffs on behalf of a putative class of similarly situated persons. The allegations in the complaint relate to a security incident experienced by one of its customer. The Company provided the customer with outsourced staffing for an employee help desk (“Service Desk”). The complaint alleges that, in the incident, a threat actor misled the Service Desk agents into resetting passwords of employee accounts that were then used by the threat actors to access and exfiltrate a copy of the customer’s loyalty database of its clients (“Database”). The complaint mischaracterizes the terms of the Company’s engagement by the customer, the Company’s role with respect to the Database, and the responsibilities undertaken by the Company’s Service Desk agents. The Company did not provide core cybersecurity threat, protection, detection, or remediation services for the customer, did not have access to or responsibility for the Database, and had no role in managing or administering it.

Meaning of Internal Financial Controls With Reference to Consolidated Financial Statements

Meaning of Internal Financial Controls With Reference to Consolidated Financial Statements
A company’s internal financial control with reference to consolidated financial statements is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. A company’s internal financial control with reference to consolidated financial statements includes those policies and procedures that (1) pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the company; (2) provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the company are being made only in accordance with authorisations of management and directors of the company; and (3) provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorised acquisition, use, or disposition of the company’s assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.
Auditor’s Responsibility

Auditor’s Responsibility
Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the Holding Company’s internal financial controls with reference to consolidated financial statements based on our audit. We conducted our audit in accordance with the Guidance Note on Audit of Internal Financial Controls Over Financial Reporting (the “Guidance Note”) and the Standards on Auditing, specified under section 143(10) of the Act, to the extent applicable to an audit of internal financial controls, both, issued by ICAI. Those Standards and the Guidance Note require that we comply with ethical requirements and plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether adequate internal financial controls with reference to consolidated financial statements was established and maintained and if such controls operated effectively in all material respects.
Inherent Limitations of Internal Financial Controls With Reference to Consolidated Financial Statements

Inherent Limitations of Internal Financial Controls With Reference to Consolidated Financial Statements
Because of the inherent limitations of internal financial controls with reference to consolidated financial statements, including the possibility of collusion or improper management override of controls, material misstatements due to error or fraud may occur and not be detected. Also, projections of any evaluation of the internal financial controls with reference to consolidated financial statements to future periods are subject to the risk that the internal financial controls with reference to consolidated financial statements may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.

(i) Functional and presentation currency
Items included in the Consolidated financial statements of each of the Group’s entities are measured using the currency of the primary economic environment in which the entity operates (the ‘functional currency’). For each entity, the Group determines the functional currency and items included in the Consolidated financial statements of each entity are measured using that functional currency. Consolidated financial statements of the Group are presented in Indian Rupee (INR/Rs.), which is the parent Company’s functional and the Group’s presentation currency.
• Impairment of trade receivables

• Impairment of trade receivables
Goodwill arising on acquisition of control is determined as per the business combination accounting policy [Refer note 1(r)]. The Group combines the Consolidated financial statements of the parent and its subsidiaries line by line by adding together like items of assets, liabilities, equity, income and expenses. Intercompany transactions, balances and unrealized gains on transactions between group companies are eliminated. Unrealized losses are also eliminated unless the transaction provides evidence of an impairment of the transferred asset. Accounting policies / different accounting period end of subsidiaries have been changed where necessary to ensure consistency with the policies / accounting period adopted by the Group.

The impairment provisions of financial assets are based on assumptions about risk of default and expected timing of collection. The Group uses judgment in making these assumptions and selecting the inputs to the expected credit loss calculation based on the Group’s history of collections, customer’s creditworthiness, existing market conditions as well as forward looking estimates at the end of each reporting period. The Group uses a provision matrix to calculate ECLs for trade receivables and contract assets. The provision rates are based on days past due for groupings of various customer segments that have similar loss patterns (i.e., by geography, product type, customer type and rating, and coverage by letters of credit and other forms of credit insurance).
• Useful lives of property, plant and equipment
The Group reviews the useful life of property, plant and equipment at the end of each reporting period. This reassessment may result in change in depreciation expense in future periods. (Refer note 1(k))
• Defined benefit plans and compensated absences

• Defined benefit plans and compensated absences
The cost of the defined benefit plans, compensated absences and the present value of the defined benefit obligations are based on actuarial valuation using the projected unit credit method. An actuarial valuation involves making various assumptions that may differ from actual developments in the future. These include the determination of the discount rate, future salary increases and mortality rates. Due to the complexities involved in the valuation and its long term nature, a defined benefit obligation is highly sensitive to changes in these assumptions. All assumptions are reviewed at each reporting date.

Cash flow hedging reserve
The Group uses hedging instruments as part of its management of foreign currency risk associated with its highly probable forecasted transactions, i.e., revenue, as described within Note 28. For hedging foreign currency risk, the Group uses Foreign Currency Forward Contracts which are designated as Cash Flow Hedges. To the extent these hedges are effective; the change in fair value of the hedging instrument is recognized in the Cash Flow Hedging Reserve. Amount recognized in the Cash Flow Hedging Reserve is reclassified to profit or loss when the hedged item effects profit and loss, under Revenue from operations.

(e) Unrecognised temporary differences

(e) Unrecognised temporary differences
As per the provisions of Section 80M of Income Tax Act, 1961, it allows the removal of cascading effect of taxes on inter-corporate dividends. Accordingly, certain subsidiaries of the Group have undistributed earnings, which are expected to be distributed as dividends, subject to tax in the hands of the Company. In accordance with the Group’s policy of further distributing dividends to its shareholders on receipt from the subsidiaries and basis prevalent tax laws i.e., section 80M, which permits offsetting of dividend received from subsidiaries with its dividend paid while computing the taxable dividend income, no liability has been recorded on such undistributed earnings.
Considering that the enactment of the Labour Codes is non‑recurring in nature, the Company has presented the incremental impact as “Impact of Labour Codes” under Exceptional Item in the consolidated financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2026. The Group continues to monitor developments relating to the Labour Codes and will evaluate the impact, if any, on the measurement of liabilities pertaining to employee benefits.

Consolidated revenue for the quarter stood at US$592.2 million in US dollar terms. In
Indian-rupee terms, revenue stood at ₹55,277 million. These figures include two months of

On an organic constant-currency basis, Banking and Financial Services grew 2.9%
sequentially and now contributes 24.7% of consolidated revenue; Insurance grew 4.6%

21.3%; and Healthcare and Hi-Tech grew 11.6% and contributes 17.3%. Government

remained our largest revenue contributor at 50%, followed by Data and Integration at 21%

surrounding architecture and the way the work gets delivered. Pilots run in controlled
conditions that mask the structural issues production really exposes. We have closed
this gap with two things built together.
• Number one, a reference architecture. designed for production-grade behavior,

Our reference architecture enforces deterministic guardrails around probabilistic LLM
outputs, solving the two failure moats that trap clients in pilots, hallucinated domain
logic, and lost agent coherence in long-running processes. This architecture, the

logic, and lost agent coherence in long-running processes. This architecture, the
reference architecture, has three layers.
• The top layer is called the business architecture layer and consists of business goals,
high-impact use cases, and organizational change management, or the OCM-led
operating model redesign.
• The middle layer is the decisioning engine, or the decisioning atlas, which is a
differentiated proprietary asset that enforces domain-specific reasoning chains with

across multi-step agentic workflows.
• The bottom layer is a composable AI backbone, swappable with hyperscalers
compute or a sovereign AI cloud or any model provider. It also contains an AI
gateway used for model routing, a model context protocol, that's called the MCP
gateway, token ops, and the ability to do canary releases in AI deployments.
We have operationalized this reference architecture with our proprietary AI ModSquads
and the forward-deployed engineers, also called as the FDEs.
In ModSquads, we implement agent harnesses for long-running, durable agents. The
harness or the scaffolding has a RAG loop with planner, generator, and evaluator agents
all tied together with guardrails or contracts and anti-leniency or adversarial patterns by
